THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:

ORDER Petitioner is before this Court with a prayer to quash the entire proceedings in Spl.CC No.567/2018 pending before the Court of Addl. City Civil and Sessions Judge, Bengaluru, arising out of Crime No.119/2017 registered by Kothanuru police station, Bengaluru for offence under Sections 363, 366,
376 of IPC and Sections 4, 6 and 10 of POCSO Act, 2012.
2.

entities.text: Addl. City Civil and Sessions Judge, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 submit that the petitioner and the victim are now married and from the wedlock a male child is born on 10.08.2020.
The petitioner and respondent No.2 are residing as husband and wife ever since the date of their marriage.
The elders of both the family had participated in the NC: 2024:KHC:10621 marriage.
They submit that the pries are not intending to continue the impugned criminal proceedings before the trial Court which is at the stage of recording evidence.
They submit that complainant, victim and other material witnesses have not supported the case of the prosecution and they have been treated as hostile witnesses.
The victim girl is presently pregnant and pendency of the criminal case is causing stress to the family.
Accordingly they pray that the application filed by the parties for compounding may be allowed and consequently the entire proceedings, which is pending before the trial Court may be quashed.
4. Learned HCGP however has opposed the petition.
He submits that undisputedly the victim was a minor at the time of alleged offence and petitioner has been charge sheeted for serious offences.

Therefore even if there is a settlement, since the alleged offences are non-compoundable in nature,
the relief sought for in the petition cannot be granted.

5. FIR in Crime No.119/2017 was registered by Kothanuru Police Station, Bengaluru, on the complaint of the second respondent herein who is the mother of the victim girl initially NC:
2024:KHC:10621 for offence under Section 363 of IPC.

During the course of investigation the police Indresh K vs State Of Karnataka on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105656964/
2 had apprehended the petitioner and the victim girl from the house of the petitioner.

sentences.text: As per the material on record the victim girl was born on 21.5.2000.
As on the date of complaint she had completed 17years of age.

The victim girl in her statement recorded during the course of investigation has stated that she was acquainted with the petitioner and after her mother who is the complainant in the present case came to know about the same she had advised her not to roam around with the petitioner.
She has also stated that elders of the petitioner had come to her house with a proposal of her marriage with the petitioner, which was rejected by her mother.
Thereafter she was not been allowed by her mother to go out of the house.

It is in this background she had left her house and had gone to the house of the petitioner and after her mother came to know about the same, a complaint was lodged and she was brought back.
6.
The petitioner has been examined before the trial Court as PW.1 and her mother who is the defacto complainant is examined as PW.2.

PWs.1 and 2 have turned hostile to the NC:
2024:KHC:10621 prosecution case and though they were cross examined by the prosecutor nothing has been elicited from their mouth.
7. Learned counsel for the parties have today filed a memo producing the birth certificate of the child born to the petitioner and second respondent herein on 10.08.2020.
It is stated in the joint affidavit filed by the petitioner, respondent No.2 and the victim, that the victim is presently pregnant by three months.

In paragraphs 1 to 4 of the joint affidavit filed by the parties it is stated as follows:
" 1. On the strength of the complaint dated 20.06.2017 lodged by CW-1/PW-1 Smt.
Kemadevi W/o Joshi, the 1st respondent have registered the case in Crime No.119/2017 for the offences punishable under Section 363 of IPC against the petitioner.

The allegations in the complaint are that, the complainant's daughter aged about 17 years, studying in 1st year B.Com at R.C. College, Bengaluru, at that time the accused Indreesh was came into contact with her and both of them were fallen in love.

On 19.06.2017 around 2.00 PM accused persuaded minor victim, the daughter of defacto complainant on the guess of marrying her an taken her to his elder sister Seema's house NC: 2024:KHC:10621 situated at Telecom Layout, and by making the victim stayed in his sister's house.
Hence, the complaint.
During the course of investigation the IO's secured the victim girl and recorded her statement and she was subjected to medial examination on 26.6.2017 at about 2.54 PM,

as per the history of victim knows the accused from 6 months and they had sexual intercourse and last such act was 2 days back, the age of victim is show as 17 years, as per medical report,
her hymen is not intact and she is sued to an act like that of sexual intercourse, even victim statement came to be recorded before the counselor at special ward of Bowring hospital, wherein she has stated that accused taken her to his elder sister's house,
wherein they were staying together for 6 days, they were also having physical relationship with each other and she is one month pregnant.
She like to go along with her mother and listen to her.
After investigation IO has filed the charge sheet for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376 of IPC ad Sections 4, 6 & 10 of POCSO Act.

sentences.text: During the course of trial the PW-1 who is the complainant and also mother / PW-1 Kemadevi, the victim girl has turned hostile and PW-1 Aishwarya - victim girl has also turned hostile.

Both petitioner and PW-1 got married and out of their wedlock PW- NC: 2024:KHC:10621 1 has given birth of male baby on 10.08.2020 (Master Ayush),
presently aged about 3 years and PW-2 has become three months pregnant and considering to restart our lives together with new beginning.

3. Under these circumstances, the 2nd respondent / PW-2 and PW-1 - Aishwarya - victim girl are not interested to prosecute the case against the petitioner and we seeks lave of this Hon'ble Court to be permit to compound the aforesaid offences and to save the life of family.

If not we will be put to untold misery.
4.
We state that, the averments made in paras 1 to 3 accompanying application are true to the best of our knowledge, information and belief.

"
8. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab reported in (2012) 10 SCC 303

entities.text: Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab reported in (2012) 10 SCC 303
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: has held

that power under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. is required to be exercised to secure the ends of justice and to prevent abuse of process of Court and these powers can be exercised to quash the legal proceedings or complaint or FIR in appropriate cases where the parties have settled their dispute and for that NC: 2024:KHC:10621 purpose any definite category of offence cannot be prescribed.

In the case of Parbatbhai Aahir vs. State of Gujarat reported in (2017) 9 SCC 641 the Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed that the powers under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. are not restricted by the provisions outlined under Section 320 of Cr.P.C., which means, the High Court can exercise its inherent powers independently notwithstanding the limitations under Section 320 of Cr.P.C.

entities.text: Parbatbhai Aahir vs. State of Gujarat reported in (2017) 9 SCC 641
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A coordinate bench of this Court in almost identical circumstances in the case of Mohammad Waseem Ahamad vs. State reported in AIR Online 2022 KAR 314, in view of the settlement arrived between the parties after the accused and the victim got married and the victim had given birth to a child, has quashed the entire proceedings in the criminal case which was pending before the special Court for similar offences.

entities.text: Mohammad Waseem Ahamad vs. State reported in AIR Online 2022 KAR 314
entities.label: PRECEDENT

In the case of Aarush Jain vs. State of Karnataka and another (Crl.P. No.3710/2022 DD 09.09.2022) a coordinate bench of this Court has observed as follows:
" xxxxxxxxxxx It is an admitted fact that the petitioner and the victim were close friends and were infatuated to each other.

entities.text: Aarush Jain vs. State of Karnataka and another (Crl.P. No.3710/2022 DD 09.09.2022)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Several Courts as NC: 2024:KHC:10621 quoted hereinabove have considered the impact of hauling an under aged boy into the web of the provisions under the POCSO Act has clearly held that POCSO Act was not meant to punish the accused who were in love with the victims therein.

[
14. It is a known fact which bear consideration in the aforequoted judgments, in physiological parlance, that adolescence of a child is between 10 to 19 years and young age is said to be between 20 to 24 years.

Therefore, adolescence is a continuum Indresh K vs State Of Karnataka on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105656964/
4 of development process in the life of a child metamorphosing into young age or an adult.

entities.text: Indresh K vs State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It would not be inapt to notice that young children or boys who have not yet reached the age of 18 years, many a time, without realizing or being ignorant of the consequences of their act which they perform in the frenzy of youth, emerge themselves as offenders under the provisions of POCSO Act and face serious consequences.
Romantic love between a boy and a girl of the age of adolescence sometimes arising out of infatuations result in the boy embroiling himself into the vortex of the provisions of the POCSO Act.

15. The laudable object for which the POCSO Act was brought into effect cannot be forgotten, but that would not mean that it is meant to punish - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:10621 young children who would fall in love and commit such acts which would become punishable under the Act, a caveat, this Court is not painting every incidence of sexual activity of any kind that would become an offence under the POCSO Act, with the same brush, but there are cases of the kind, like the one at hand,
where the adolescents have indulged in such acts due to lack of knowledge of consequence of law.
xxxxxxxxxxxx

" 
9. No doubt Section 376 of IPC and Sections 4 and 6 of the POCSO Act are non-compoundable under Section 320 of Cr.P.C., however, considering the observation made by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Gian Singh and Parbatbhai, that the powers of the High Court under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. are not restricted by the provisions of Section 320 of Cr.P.C. and the inherent powers under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. can be exercised to quash the FIR or criminal proceedings if this Court is of the considered opinion that continuation of the criminal case is not in the interest of the parties and on the other hand ends of justice would be secured if the criminal proceedings is quashed

,
notwithstanding the fact - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:10621 that alleged offences are non compoundable, still this Court in deserving cases can quash the entire proceedings.
10. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ramgopal and another vs. State Of Madhya Pradesh reported in AIR 2022 (14) SCC 531 has held

entities.text: Ramgopal and another vs. State Of Madhya Pradesh reported in AIR 2022 (14) SCC 531
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
that even in cases involving non compoundable offences where compromise is arrived post conviction, extra ordinary powers of the High Court can be exercised beyond the metes and bounds of Section 320 of Cr.P.C.
11.

The High Court while exercising its power under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. in a case involving non-compoundable offence is required to take into consideration the gravity of offences and also the nature of offence.

If the alleged offences are purely private in nature and if it is between the close family members and if a settlement is arrived between the parties who are close family members Indresh K vs State Of Karnataka on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105656964/
5 who intend to give a quietus to all the disputes, can quash such criminal proceedings.

entities.text: Indresh K vs State Of Karnataka on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The High Court is required to exercise such discretion taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the case surrounding the incident and also the background in which the settlement has - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:10621 been arrived between the parties having regard to the nature of the offences and the conduct of the accused before and after the incident.

Under the circumstances, I am of the opinion that this is a fit case wherein the inherent powers of this Court under Section 482 of Cr.P.C.
is required to be exercised to do complete justice to the parties who are before this Court.
Accordingly, the following - ORDER The Criminal petition is allowed.

The entire proceedings in Spl.CC No.567/2018 pending before the Court of Addl. City Civil and Sessions Judge, Bengaluru, arising out of Crime No.119/2017 registered by Kothanuru police station, Bengaluru for offence under Sections 363, 366, 376 of IPC and Sections 4, 6 and 10 of POCSO Act, 2012, stands quashed.
